title: Add offline econ prober and quant preset importer to SDK (local-sim tooling)
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: teams frequently iterate on prefill/batching/quant profiles but lack a lightweight way to run unit-econ simulations locally before pushing changes to the platform. This PR adds an offline prober and quant preset importer to the Python SDK so devs can: 1) run fast local simulations against sampled workloads, 2) import/validate quantization YAMLs produced by the model tooling, and 3) generate a compact cost delta report to guide conservative rollout decisions. Motivation: reduce deploy-retry cycles, catch regressions in cost/latency tradeoffs earlier, and make onboarding for non-infra engineers simpler. What changed: added redwood.econ.offline.Prober and redwood.econ.importer. The prober accepts sample sets (JSONL/ndjson) and runs a simulated batching/cache pipeline with configurable SLO and token distributions; it reports token-level unit-econ, cold/cached latency deltas, and a risk score for aggressive quant settings. The importer validates quant preset YAMLs (structure, supported ops, target bitwidths) and emits a normalized preset that matches the platform schema (but does not auto-deploy). Safety: telemetry is opt-in; by default runs in dry-run mode and warns when presets would cause >5% estimated perplexity delta (requires an eval anchor). Backwards compatibility: zero-impact on existing APIs unless users explicitly import and call the new classes. Included docstrings, a short quickstart in README, and a test harness with small synthetic samples. Checklist: - [x] CLI bindings: redwood econ probe/import (shim to SDK) - [x] Importer validation + normalization - [x] Local simulation engine with simple batching model - [x] Unit tests for importer and prober - [x] README quickstart and example sample files - [x] Security review (no network calls by default) - [x] End-to-end smoke run on CI Design notes: the simulator models batching using a configurable window/timeout heuristic and supports per-request token-length distributions. The risk score combines estimated unit-econ delta, latency tail amplification, and a simple quality proxy (if eval anchors provided). Limitations: this is a lightweight estimator and is not a replacement for full tenant-sim runs in the control plane. Migration: none required; consumers can opt into the new API. Example usage: 1) redwood econ probe samples.ndjson --preset local_qs.yaml --slo 50ms 2) from redwood.econ import offline; Prober(...).run("samples.ndjson", preset="local_qs.yaml") Testing & results: synthetic smoke across 3 sample sets shows estimated token cost changes within 8% of platform sim for small models (reconciled by downstream tenant-sim). Shipping notes: add to SDK changelog under "Tooling", callout in release announcement for Platform/SEs.
